  "agent": "The President",

  "situation": "In September 1945, the President faced a decision about the Office of Strategic Services as the country shifted from wartime to peacetime. The nation and Congress favored rapid demobilization, and the OSS faced major reductions. Congress had imposed a funding requirement on new agencies operating for more than 12 months. At the same time, senior officials believed the country needed some form of permanent intelligence establishment, while assessments of the OSS and its proposed reforms included serious criticism. The available courses included ending the OSS and transferring its functions to other departments, or retaining it as a peacetime intelligence agency.",
  "question": "What should the President do about the Office of Strategic Services as the country shifts to peacetime?",
  "facts": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "The nation and Congress wanted rapid demobilization after the war, and the OSS was marked for major reductions because many of its personnel served in wartime functions considered extraneous in peacetime.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "kind": "authority",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "A law passed in early 1945 required the White House to seek a specific Congressional appropriation for any new agency operating for longer than 12 months.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "Congress regarded the OSS as a temporary war agency that would need to be wound down after victory.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "kind": "intelligence",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "An informal investigation criticized the OSS for poor performance and lax security and characterized its proposed intelligence reform as resembling an authoritarian secret-police system.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.2", "src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "kind": "intelligence",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "The investigation recommended abolishing the OSS while allowing some personnel and activities to be preserved in other agencies.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F6",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "Many senior officials believed the country needed a permanent intelligence establishment, and the Budget Bureau had begun studying intelligence needs and possible reforms with presidential support.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F7",
      "kind": "capability",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "Wartime intelligence success was understood to have depended chiefly on cryptologic successes, with the OSS playing a supporting role.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p28.6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F8",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "The OSS director insisted that a permanent intelligence service report directly to the President and refused to compromise with Joint Chiefs representatives studying postwar intelligence needs.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p29.3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F9",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "The Budget Bureau initially contemplated a gradual liquidation of the OSS that would preserve valuable assets while releasing personnel and ending functions no longer needed in peacetime.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p30.1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F10",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "Senior presidential advisers recommended dissolving the OSS almost immediately.",
      "spans": ["src:37eafef6ba8f#p30.1"]
    }
  ],

      "do": "The President should dissolve the OSS and transfer its functions to the State and War Departments.",

    }
